title: SK hynix HBM4
summary: The next generation of high-bandwidth memory, with a wider interface and higher stacks.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

HBM4 widens the memory interface to 2,048 bits and stacks more DRAM dies, which raises bandwidth per accelerator and shifts packaging difficulty onto the memory maker. SK hynix, the incumbent HBM leader, has targeted mass production around 2026, with custom base dies that let accelerator designers tune the memory to their chip. Supply is constrained by stacking yield and by advanced packaging capacity.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2026–2028
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Whoever qualifies first on HBM4 sets the ramp schedule for the next accelerator generation, so qualification news is capacity news.

What Would Change The View

  • Qualification by major accelerator vendors.
  • Stack yield and thermal behaviour.
  • Custom base-die business model.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
